title: Complex harmonic identification of loss-factor damping
source: The single-degree-of-freedom impedance is Z=k−omega²m+i eta k and u=F/Z. At k=4 N/m, m=1 kg, omega=1 rad/s and eta=0.5, u=3/13−2i/13 m. The recipe stores frequency in Hz as 1/(2 pi), so the solver's angular frequency is omega=1 rad/s; the derivative du/deta=−i k/Z² gives the local interval from two independent Cartesian errors.

quantities.reason: The observed real and imaginary components are the exact impedance response at eta=0.5.
With 1e-4 m independent real/imaginary errors, the scalar information is |du/deta|²/sigma²; the endpoint is eta−1.959963984540054 sigma_eta.
The same Cartesian-error linearization gives eta+1.959963984540054 sigma_eta.
